macro: The macro backdrop remains uncertain, with IPO market conditions deteriorating as multiple high-profile offerings are being delayed or imploding post-debut. The troubled macro landscape had investors bracing for weak consumer-facing results heading into today's session. Risk sentiment is being tested by questions around whether major private tech companies can achieve anticipated IPO timelines and valuations.
market_outlook: No explicit directional index call is made in this note. The key catalyst to watch is whether the KMX blowout signals broader used auto and consumer resilience, versus the IPO market stress signaling tighter financial conditions ahead.
bull_case: CarMax delivered a massive earnings blowout, beating EPS by over 43 cents and revenue by nearly $850 million, suggesting the consumer may be more resilient than feared. Turnaround initiatives are clearly gaining traction, with credit income, unit volumes, and protection plan revenue all accelerating. Management's decision to resume share buybacks signals internal confidence in the business trajectory.
bear_case: The IPO market is showing serious stress, with Oura joining SB Energy and Holtec in delaying offerings, and Shein shares imploding after its Hong Kong debut. This raises serious questions about whether Anthropic and OpenAI can go public on schedule and at expected valuations, which is critical because those IPOs are seen as key drivers of ongoing data center and AI capex spending. A stalled AI IPO pipeline could ripple negatively through the entire data center and hyperscaler ecosystem.

company_items.summary: CarMax reported a massive FQ2 beat with EPS of $1.16 versus the Street at $0.73, an 81.3% upside surprise, on revenue of $7.9 billion versus estimates of $7.05 billion, up 19.5% year-over-year. The beat was broad-based: used vehicle units rose 13.8%, ASPs up 6.3%, extended protection plan revenue up 23%, and CarMax Auto Finance income rose 32.1% to $135.6 million on lower provisions. Management is resuming share repurchases this quarter and has scheduled an analyst day for November 3rd.

Oura announced this morning it is postponing its IPO citing uncertainty in the IPO market, becoming the latest in a string of delayed offerings alongside SB Energy and Holtec. This follows the implosion in Shein shares after its Hong Kong debut and adds to growing concern that Anthropic and OpenAI may struggle to go public on their anticipated timelines and at expected valuations. The potential delay of those two marquee AI IPOs is significant because they are viewed as critical catalysts for continued data center capital expenditure.

sectors: Used auto retail is showing surprising strength based on KMX results, contradicting cautious signals from AutoNation at a recent conference. The IPO market is under meaningful stress, with implications for AI and data center capex if Anthropic and OpenAI listings get pushed out.
tts_summary: Here's your morning read for September 29th. The headline this morning is a blowout from CarMax, and separately, more trouble in the IPO market that has real implications for the AI trade. Let's get into it. CarMax crushed fiscal second quarter expectations across the board. EPS came in at a dollar sixteen versus the Street at seventy-three cents — that's an eighty-one percent upside surprise. Revenue hit seven point nine billion against estimates of seven point zero five billion, up nearly twenty percent year over year. The beat was not a one-line story. Used vehicle units were up nearly fourteen percent, average selling prices up over six percent, extended protection plan revenue up twenty-three percent, and CarMax Auto Finance income jumped thirty-two percent to a hundred thirty-five point six million dollars, helped by lower loan loss provisions. Management is resuming share buybacks this quarter after pausing them for several months, and they've scheduled an analyst day for November third. This is a clean, broad-based beat. Coming into the print, AutoNation had made cautious remarks at a recent conference, so the bar was low — and CarMax cleared it easily. The turnaround initiatives are bearing fruit, and this result suggests the used auto consumer is holding up better than feared. Now the other story this morning is more concerning. If the IPO window stays closed or unstable, those listings get pushed out — and that raises real questions about the timeline and valuation assumptions underpinning the entire AI infrastructure buildout. For the session today, CarMax is a clear positive, and could lift sentiment around used autos and consumer durability. But the IPO market stress and its downstream implications for AI capex is a genuine headwind for data center names, hyperscalers, and anything tied to the AI spending cycle. Watch how the market weighs those two competing signals. The macro backdrop remains unsettled — no rates or Fed commentary in this note — so price action off the open will tell you a lot about where conviction sits heading into the end of the quarter.
